job.style: a conversation between a teacher and two students

passage: Teacher: Today, let us discuss the nature of matter. Rohan, if you mix salt and water, is the resulting solution a pure substance? Rohan: Yes, because I cannot see any different parts in it, so it must be pure. Teacher: Not quite, Rohan. A mixture like salt water looks uniform, but it is not a pure substance because it can be separated by physical methods. Priya: What about alloys like brass? Since I cannot see the zinc and copper separately, is brass a compound? Teacher: That is a common confusion, Priya. Alloys are mixtures because they retain the properties of their components and can be separated, unlike compounds. Priya: I see. So, if I have a compound like water, can I use filtration to separate it into hydrogen and oxygen? Teacher: No, compounds are chemically bonded. You cannot use physical methods like filtration to separate a compound into its constituent elements. Finally, remember that solutions are not always liquid. Air is a solution of gases, and it remains a mixture even if it looks clear. When we evaporate a salt solution, the water turns to gas, but the salt remains behind as a solid residue. The salt does not disappear or turn into gas during the process.

items.evidence: A mixture like salt water looks uniform, but it is not a pure substance because it can be separated by physical methods.
items.q: Salt water looks the same all through. Why is it still not a pure substance?
options: Its salt and water can be split apart physically
Its salt has vanished completely into the water
Its salt and water are bonded into a compound
Its salt grains can be seen if we look closely
items.explain: Salt water looks uniform, but physical methods can separate it, so it is a mixture.

wrong.why: thinks dissolving makes a new compound
ignores that the passage says it looks uniform

items.evidence: Alloys are mixtures because they retain the properties of their components and can be separated, unlike compounds.
items.q: Priya cannot see zinc and copper separately in brass. What kind of substance is brass?
options: A mixture, as its metals keep their properties
A compound, as its metals cannot be seen
A pure element, as it looks fully uniform
A pure substance, as it melts at one temperature
items.explain: Brass is an alloy, and alloys are mixtures because zinc and copper keep their own properties.

wrong.why: thinks a uniform look means pure
thinks mixtures have a fixed melting point

items.evidence: You cannot use physical methods like filtration to separate a compound into its constituent elements.
items.q: Priya pours water through filter paper. What happens to the hydrogen and oxygen in it?
options: They stay joined, as filtering cannot break bonds
They separate, as filtering can split compounds
They separate, as water is only a mixture
They stay joined, but boiling would split them
items.explain: Water is a compound; its elements are chemically bonded, so filtration cannot separate them.

wrong.why: thinks water is a mixture of two gases
thinks boiling or distilling can split a compound

items.evidence: Air is a solution of gases, and it remains a mixture even if it looks clear.
items.q: Air looks clear to us. What kind of matter is it really?
options: A solution made of several gases
A pure substance, since it looks uniform
A compound of gases bonded together
A gas mixture, but not a solution
items.explain: Air is a solution of gases. It stays a mixture even though it looks clear.

wrong.why: thinks a uniform look means pure
thinks mixed gases form a compound

items.evidence: When we evaporate a salt solution, the water turns to gas, but the salt remains behind as a solid residue.
items.q: Salt water is heated until all its water evaporates. What is left behind?
options: Solid salt, left behind as a residue
Nothing, as the salt also turns to gas
Pure water, as the salt escapes first
A new compound of salt and water
items.explain: Only the water turns to gas; the salt stays behind as a solid residue.

wrong.why: thinks the solute turns into gas too
reverses which part turns to gas
thinks salt and water formed a compound
